c.tagline: Where Mediterranean blue meets ancient Carthage stone.

taxi.fareNote: Meter starts around 4.70 TND by day (7.05 TND 21:00-06:00, a 50% night surcharge); insist drivers use the meter. Airport taxis instead charge a fixed fare of roughly 30-35 TND to downtown.

emergency.note: 198 reaches Protection Civile (fire/rescue); response times can be slow outside central areas, tourist hotels can usually assist in English/French.

hood_landmark.Les Berges du Lac: Lac de Tunis, Les Berges du Lac 2

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the medina and along Ave Habib Bourguiba; caution at night

hood_desc: Tunis's UNESCO-listed old city of narrow souks, mosques and centuries-old townhouses; best for culture-focused travelers who want to be immersed in history and don't mind noise and tourist bustle.

The 19th-century colonial-era new town centered on Avenue Habib Bourguiba, with cafes, banks and the widest choice of budget-to-midrange hotels; suits first-timers who want a central, walkable base near transit.
A modern lakeside business district of glass towers, malls and international hotel chains; suits business travelers and those wanting quiet, contemporary comfort away from the old city crowds.

An iconic blue-and-white clifftop village overlooking the Gulf of Tunis, full of cafes and art galleries; suits couples and photographers wanting a boutique, laid-back coastal stay a short train ride from downtown.
An upscale beachfront resort district north of the city with 5-star hotels and calm sandy coves; suits travelers who want resort-style relaxation with easy taxi access into central Tunis.
lodging: Radisson Blu Hotel & Convention Center, Tunis

water.note: Sources conflict on safety; high mineral content can upset visitors' stomachs, so bottled water is the safer choice.

transit.pay: Buy paper tickets or cards at station kiosks/vending machines for the Métro léger and TGM before boarding; city buses are typically paid in small cash to the conductor or with a Transtu card. There is no unified rechargeable card covering all modes for tourists.
transit.hours: Métro léger and buses run roughly 05:00-24:00 with reduced late-night frequency; the TGM runs about 05:00-00:00. There is no true all-night service, so use taxis or Yassir after midnight.
transit.note: Together the light rail, TGM coastal train and bus network cover Greater Tunis including La Marsa, Sidi Bou Said and Carthage; services can be crowded and schedules loosely kept, so allow extra time.

ferry: CTN ferries to Marseille and Genoa from La Goulette/Rades port

transit.m: SNT public bus to city center (30-45 min)

tip.r: 10-15% at sit-down restaurants is standard since service staff rely on tips; round up for taxis; not expected at cafe counters, bars, or hotel front desks.
